title: On Fear and Leadership: Product to Sales CTOs & CEOs

reader_summary.headline: Hi, everyone, welcome to the A6&Z podcast.
reader_summary.overview: Hi, everyone, welcome to the A6&Z podcast. I'm Sonal, and in this episode, part of our ongoing founder operator series, which you can find more of at A6NC.com slash founder stories. The conversation took place as a hallway style chat and features A6 and Z general partner Martine Casado, who co-founded and was CET.

key_points.text: I'm Sonal, and in this episode, part of our ongoing founder operator series.
key_points.evidence_quote: I'm Sonal, and in this episode, part of our ongoing founder operator series, which you can find more of at A6NC.com slash founder stories, is about founders wrestling with how to evolve their roles from product to sales, and the question of bringing in an external CEO or not.

key_points.text: The conversation took place as a hallway style chat and features A6 and Z general partner Martine Casado, who co-founded and was CET.
key_points.evidence_quote: The conversation took place as a hallway style chat and features A6 and Z general partner Martine Casado, who co-founded and was CET, CEO of NICERRA and shared his own journey, lessons learned, and advice for founders at A6NZ.com slash external CEO.

key_points.text: And then the voice you'll hear after both of ours is Armand Dadgar, the co-founder and CTO of cloud infrastructure automation company, Hashikorp.
key_points.evidence_quote: And then the voice you'll hear after both of ours is Armand Dadgar, the co-founder and CTO of cloud infrastructure automation company, Hashikorp, which enables enterprises to provision, secure, connect, and run any infrastructure for any application.

key_points.text: And while the two share their own journeys, our conversation is really more broadly about the phases that all leaders and startups go through.
key_points.evidence_quote: And while the two share their own journeys, our conversation is really more broadly about the phases that all leaders and startups go through, though they may end up in different places.

thesis: The speakers argue that startups evolve through three distinct leadership phases: the product phase focused on finding product-market fit, the sales phase focused on building a repeatable go-to-market motion with good unit economics, and the operation phase focused on scaling via mechanisms like channel engagement and M&A. They suggest that while these phases can be led by the same founder undergoing a significant personal metamorphosis, they often require different personality types, such as a pioneer, a town settler, and a city planner, to effectively navigate each stage.
